description:
FILED s532d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08), found by #3830's probes.  PRE-EXISTING (base 06a4b8ba the same).

perl's scalar() only imposes scalar context: it returns the SV, so an aliasing consumer (a sub's @_, foreach) sees the variable itself.  PCL's p-scalar returns the VALUE (`(stringp v) v`), so the alias is lost:
    sub app { $_[0] .= "Z" } my $x = "a"; app(scalar($x)); print "$x\n";            # perl aZ, PCL a
    my %h = (k => "b"); app(scalar($h{k})); print "$h{k}\n";                          # perl bZ, PCL b
(probe scratch/s532d/pr/sc.pl in the s532d worktree).  s532d made p-scalar answer a PRIVATE-BUFFER box (:strbuf / :memfh) as itself, so that one shape aliases like perl now (ir-spec "in-place .=", #3830); a dualvar box already did.  Every `($)` prototype slot is a p-scalar, so a user sub with a `$` prototype that writes $_[0] is the shape that matters.  FIX SHAPE (not designed): return the box for any scalar BOX that is not a reference wrapper when the consumer aliases; the copy for a value consumer is what box-set already does.  Measure the `($)`-slot rows (Pl/t grep `proto`) first: returning the box changes what a `($)` callee's @_ holds.
subject: scalar(EXPR) copies a plain scalar where perl passes the SV itself: `sub f { $_[0] .= "Z" } my $x = "a"; f(scalar($x)); print $x` is aZ in perl, a in PCL (also a hash element) -- silent wrong, rare
